memories.title: Backup includes three stores
memories.body: The backup command writes pages, transcripts, and a mem.db snapshot to a tar.gz archive.

memories.title: Restore validates archive members
memories.body: Restore validates archive members against path traversal and symlinks before extraction.

memories.title: Restore preserves previous store
memories.body: Restore moves the existing data into a pre-restore-<timestamp>/ directory instead of deleting it.

memories.title: Restore rebuilds search index
memories.body: The restore command rebuilds the index after replacing the store.

memories.title: Project folder from git origin
memories.body: With a usable Git origin, including enterprise or self-hosted GitLab, the readable project folder uses the repository basename with a git- prefix.

memories.title: Project folder fallback
memories.body: A local Git repository without a usable origin and a non-Git workspace use the workspace folder name.

memories.title: Project identity in front matter
memories.body: Project front matter is authoritative for the opaque project_id and safe display label; the folder is a readable locator, not the identity.

memories.title: Project folder collision fails closed
memories.body: If two folders contain the same project_id, node type, and slug, lookup and force rebuild fail closed instead of choosing one page.

memories.title: Transcript dated storage
memories.body: Transcript JSONL and metadata use dated directories under ~/.memex/transcripts/YYYY-MM-DD/.

memories.title: Transcript sidecar usage
memories.body: Token counts are metadata, not transcript content. The session .meta.json sidecar carries session totals and per-turn usage, using the latest reported values rather than summing cumulative records.

memories.title: Transcript episode provenance
memories.body: Ingestion writes a JSONL transcript and .meta.json, creates a global episode page with transcript_ref, and indexes the episode.

memories.title: Repeated Codex capture
memories.body: Repeated Codex captures merge by stable session identity so compaction and shutdown events remain idempotent.

memories.title: Viz loopback read boundary
memories.body: The optional memex viz process binds only to loopback. Every dashboard GET is read-only and must not write pages, transcripts, metadata, the index, or access counters.

memories.title: Viz untrusted rendering
memories.body: Stored memories, transcript turns, session metadata, and URL parameters are untrusted. Rendered values are escaped except AI Markdown through the existing safe renderer.

memories.title: Viz transcript path confinement
memories.body: Session IDs are validated before lookup, and resolved transcript and metadata paths must stay inside the transcript root.

memories.title: Viz fragments same rules
memories.body: Scope and project IDs select existing namespaces rather than creating paths. Direct /view/ URLs and HTMX fragments follow the same read and rendering rules.

memories.title: Verify page and index checks
memories.body: memex verify always checks that every page parses, the index matches content hashes, and every link resolves.

memories.title: Verify since activity
memories.body: With --since, memex verify reports recall activity from access telemetry and write activity from updated timestamps since the cutoff.

memories.title: Verify required evidence exit
memories.body: --require-recall and --require-write turn missing activity evidence into exit code 1.

memories.title: Copilot proof workflow
memories.body: The GitHub Copilot adapter supplies a memex verify workflow for every pull request because its hosted environment has no local hooks or stdio.

memories.title: Recall safe query tokens
memories.body: Recall reduces the query to safe alphanumeric tokens and removes known scaffolding phrases before searching.

memories.title: Recall strict then fallback
memories.body: The production semantic-and-fallback-fts5 ranker tries strict AND matching first and uses a broad OR fallback only if strict matching has no hits.

memories.title: Recall column weights
memories.body: Production SQLite FTS5 search weights slug=1, title=1, body=2, tags=1 and caps the safe query at 64 tokens and 1,024 UTF-8 bytes.

memories.title: Recall ordering and counters
memories.body: Filters apply before limiting; returned slugs are unique, ascending slug breaks final ties, and recall hits bump access counters.

memories.title: Adapter install backup
memories.body: memex install <name> ships its marketplace assets in the package. Installs are idempotent and back up existing configs.

memories.title: Adapter MCP registration
memories.body: Claude Code registers MCP with claude mcp add --scope user, Codex uses config.toml [mcp_servers], and Copilot uses .vscode/mcp.json; --no-mcp skips registration.

memories.title: Adapter uninstall boundaries
memories.body: memex uninstall <name> removes Memex hooks, MCP registration, copied adapter files, and exact guidance snippets. Unrelated settings and modified files stay in place and are reported.

memories.title: Adapter uninstall keeps data
memories.body: Removing adapters keeps ~/.memex memories, transcripts, and configuration. Removing the CLI later with uv tool uninstall memex also leaves ~/.memex data.

memories.title: Docs living versus frozen
memories.body: Current architecture, product, and user-guide documents are living and must match current reality. Accepted ADRs and shipped specs are frozen history.

memories.title: Approved spec plan pinned
memories.body: At plan approval, a spec and plan are pinned in substance; only lifecycle bookkeeping can change. Execution observations belong in notes/verification-ledger.md.

memories.title: Frozen supersession status
memories.body: A later decision that partly supersedes a frozen spec is recorded in its Status field with the superseding ADR and affected part. The frozen body is not changed.

memories.title: ADR revision by successor
memories.body: An accepted ADR is not edited when reversed. A new ADR supersedes it, and the old record changes status while its text remains history.

memories.title: Wiki pages are durable source
memories.body: Every memory is a Markdown page under ~/.memex/docs with YAML front matter and Markdown body; mem.db is a disposable BM25 index.

memories.title: Memory node categories
memories.body: Memex node types are entity, preference, procedure, summary, and episode.

memories.title: Memory write collision
memories.body: Slugs derive from titles, collisions receive -2 or -3 suffixes, and an existing slug update preserves id, created, and access counters.

memories.title: Memory status approval
memories.body: Recall and injection see active pages only unless include_inactive is selected; manual governance approval leaves consolidation-created pages pending until approved.

memories.title: Secret scrub boundaries
memories.body: CLI, MCP, transcript ingest, and consolidation writes redact credential patterns before storage and log only redaction categories.

memories.title: Consolidation explicit operation
memories.body: Consolidation is the only LLM-calling operation and runs only on explicit request; it proposes durable nodes from recent episodes.

memories.title: Injection token packing
memories.body: Hook injection has a 4096-token default budget, skips hits that do not fit, always includes the top hit whole, and stays silent below the relevance floor.

memories.title: Dashboard paging
memories.body: The Memories view presents 20 newest-first cards per page and preserves type and scope in Previous and Next URLs.

memories.title: Dashboard search mode
memories.body: Best match searches the selected project first and then falls back to all memory; Search everywhere searches all namespaces without updating access counters.

memories.title: MCP tool inventory
memories.body: The MCP server exposes five typed tools: memex_write, memex_recall, memex_consolidate, memex_forget, and memex_provenance.

memories.title: Application facade ownership
memories.body: Memex is the public Python API and composition root; adapters call the facade or shared application services.

memories.title: Source document audience
memories.body: The documentation hierarchy separates internal contributor material from external user material and distinguishes living, frozen, and governance lifecycles.

memories.title: Retired recall metadata note
memories.body: The first transcript line may be an optional session header with session id, CLI version, provider, working directory, Git branch and commit, model details, timestamps, and duration.

memories.title: Retired page status note
memories.body: memex forget with archive mode retires a page in place instead of deleting it.

memories.title: Foreign workspace backup note
memories.body: Backups carry pages and transcripts along with a mem.db snapshot.

memories.title: Foreign workspace route note
memories.body: The optional viz process binds to loopback and renders stored records as untrusted data.

tasks.name: restoration-check
tasks.goal: A contributor is adding a disaster-recovery check to the CLI. Determine the contents of a backup and the safeguards and index step that a restore check must verify.

tasks.name: project-folder-diagnosis
tasks.goal: A repository changes its Git remote and a maintainer asks whether existing project pages should move. Explain how the folder is selected, where identity lives, and what happens if duplicate pages appear.

tasks.name: session-capture-audit
tasks.goal: Trace a coding session through automatic capture and explain how a diagnostic should handle repeat captures, token accounting, storage, and provenance.

tasks.name: dashboard-route-hardening
tasks.goal: A new HTMX session fragment is planned for the local dashboard. Identify the read, rendering, path, and scope constraints its route must preserve.

tasks.name: ci-evidence-gate
tasks.goal: Prepare a Copilot pull-request check that proves stored memory health and recent read and write use. Determine which checks run by default, how to set the cutoff, and what makes the job fail.

tasks.name: recall-behavior-review
tasks.goal: Review a change to search ranking that broadens all queries and changes tie ordering. Identify the current query normalization, two-stage match behavior, weighting, and result-side effects.

tasks.name: adapter-lifecycle-test
tasks.goal: A maintainer is writing an install/uninstall regression scenario for coding-agent adapters. Specify config backup and MCP behavior, then define what uninstall removes and what it must preserve.

tasks.name: decision-document-update
tasks.goal: A shipped design decision has been partly reversed. Plan the documentation update so current behavior stays accurate without rewriting approved history or execution notes.
